statements.status_notes: CVE-2011-4116: the _is_safe() check in Perl's File::Temp module, which runs when a program raises File::Temp->safe_level to MEDIUM or HIGH, does not handle symlinks properly: a template path that passes through a symlink owned by another local user is accepted, and the returned temporary path still runs through that symlink (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2011-4116, https://bugs.debian.org/776268, upstream report https://github.com/Perl-Toolchain-Gang/File-Temp/issues/14, originally rt.cpan.org #69106). The upstream report is still open and no fix has been released. A contributor there questions the value of patching _is_safe(), because a name-based check always races with the later use of the path, and a 2026 comment asks whether a trusted patch exists, since the original patch was found insufficient. Debian lists perl 5.40.1-6+deb13u1 in trixie as vulnerable, with unimportant urgency. Both published perl-modules-5.40 builds of 5.40.1-6+deb13u1 in the DHI Debian repository ship File::Temp 0.2311 with _is_safe() unchanged. Pending a maintainer decision on whether a check that only runs when a program raises safe_level, and that upstream regards as inherently racy, is enough to record perl as not affected for every program that uses the module, or whether it stays affected until upstream changes _is_safe(), this owner stays under investigation.
